purpose: Record the GitHub main-branch merge gates that currently explain why auto-merge can be enabled while PRs remain blocked until human review requirements are satisfied.

requiredRules.whyItMatters: Auto-merge cannot complete until the required human and code-owner review gates are satisfied.
Unsigned commits can be accepted onto feature branches only when branch creation bypass is permitted, but protected main still requires signed history at merge time.
Merge commits are not acceptable for protected main history.
CodeQL must not report blocking alerts before a PR can merge.
Repository quality gates are part of the merge readiness signal.
Protected refs must not be deleted as part of normal PR work.
Force-push and non-fast-forward updates are blocked for protected refs.
Restricted branch creation requires approved actors or repository ruleset bypass.
Branch updates must satisfy repository rules before protected integration.

safeOperatorActions: Keep work on short-lived feature branches.
Open focused PRs with validation and rollback notes.
Enable auto-merge after PR creation when branch policy allows it.
Ask human reviewers to satisfy review count, code owner review, and last-push approval.
Re-run or wait for CodeQL, security, governance, and quality checks.
Do not use admin bypass unless the repository owner explicitly accepts that risk for the specific PR.

nextSafeAction: Use this contract as the human-review checklist for blocked auto-merge PRs, then continue development in independent, reviewable branches while reviewers satisfy protected-branch gates.
